name: Bosley-Salih-Alorainy syndrome
aliases: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles type 3

criteria.description: Congenital non-progressive ophthalmoplegia affecting multiple extraocular muscles
Bilateral or unilateral congenital ptosis with poor levator function
Facial nerve palsy or weakness present from birth
MRI evidence of absent or hypoplastic oculomotor and/or trochlear nerves
Mild developmental delay or intellectual disability in some cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital ophthalmoplegia with ptosis and facial nerve weakness, supported by neuroimaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by MRI; genetic testing may identify mutations in TUBB3 gene.

searchTerms: non-progressive eye movement weakness from birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital ptosis with poor levator palpebrae function

searchTerms: facial muscle weakness present at birth

common.symptomName: Strabismus due to extraocular muscle fibrosis
searchTerms: crossed eyes due to stiff eye muscles
strabismus caused by eye muscle fibrosis

common.symptomName: Hypoplasia or absence of oculomotor and trochlear nerves on MRI
searchTerms: missing or small eye movement nerves on MRI
absent oculomotor and trochlear nerves seen on scan

occasional.symptomName: Dysphagia due to cranial nerve involvement
searchTerms: swallowing issues due to cranial nerve damage
trouble eating caused by nerve dysfunction

rare.symptomName: Respiratory difficulties due to cranial nerve dysfunction
searchTerms: respiratory difficulty due to cranial nerve issues
impaired breathing control from nerve dysfunction

imaging: MRI showing hypoplasia or absence of oculomotor (III) and trochlear (IV) cranial nerves
Fibrosis of extraocular muscles on orbital imaging
other: Clinical observation of congenital ophthalmoplegia and facial nerve palsy

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly affects oculomotor nerve with ptosis but lacks facial nerve palsy
Facial and abducens nerve palsy with limb abnormalities
Absence of congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles

references: Bosley TM, Salih MA, Alorainy IA et al. Bosley-Salih-Alorainy syndrome: a distinct congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles phenotype. Am J Med Genet A. 2007.
